source.original_text: For natural d,q satisfying2q+1<d, put r=q+1, including q=0. Use Omega=(R^d)^r and the original product mu of r independent standard d-dimensional Gaussian column laws. Phi_i is the physical row with coordinates omega(b)_i. Put theta_i=(i-1/2)pi/d, t_i=(1,sqrt(2)cos(theta_i),...,sqrt(2)cos(q theta_i)), L=2r+3log(1000d), and w_i=cos((2q+1)theta_i). Define Yi=d^(-1)(Phi_i Phi_i^T tensor t_i t_i^T) on norm(Phi_i)^2<=L and zero otherwise; Mi is its actual Bochner integral under the same original unconditional mu, Zi=Yi-Mi. Put a=r^(-1) integral norm(x)^2 times the inclusive cutoff indicator under the standard r-dimensional Gaussian. Define the actual d by r^2 matrix B by B_(i,(b,k))=sqrt(d)^(-1) Phi_i(b)t_i(k), with Gaussian index first, and let G be the event that every actual row satisfies its inclusive cutoff. Authored private deterministic generalization of the Ex126 implication: for every real threshold Delta and every original sample omega, if omega belongs to G and both norm(sum_i Zi(omega))<=Delta and norm(sum_i wi Zi(omega))<=Delta, then norm(B(omega)^T B(omega)-I_(r^2))<=Delta+(1-a) and norm(B(omega)^T diag(w) B(omega))<=Delta. Norms are real Euclidean operator norms. The source numeric positive threshold is one instance; the private generalization quantifies over all real thresholds, with negative-threshold antecedents impossible. No event probability or new public API is claimed.

decoder_context: Fin n is the finite set of natural numbers strictly less than n; i.val is the zero-based natural value of i. Natural numbers embed into the reals in the usual way.

EuclideanSpace real (Fin n) is real n-dimensional Euclidean space with its Euclidean norm and Borel structure. WithLp.toLp 2 wraps a coordinate function as a Euclidean vector; WithLp.ofLp recovers its same coordinates.
stdGaussian is the centered Gaussian probability law with identity covariance. Measure.pi is the displayed finite product measure on the corresponding function space.
Real.log is the natural logarithm; Real.sqrt is the nonnegative square root. Set.indicator S f is f on S and zero off S. An if-condition written with less-than-or-equal includes equality.

Matrix is the displayed finite real matrix space. Matrix.vecMulVec u v has entry u_i v_j. Matrix.kronecker A B has entry A_(i,k) B_(j,l) at row (i,j) and column (k,l). transpose interchanges matrix indices; multiplication is ordinary matrix multiplication.

Matrix.diagonal w has diagonal entry w_i and every off-diagonal entry zero. The matrix 1 is the identity on its displayed finite index set. Scalar multiplication, subtraction and finite sums have their usual real matrix meanings.
All matrix norms use the real Euclidean L2 operator norm of the displayed matrix action; they are not entrywise or coordinate sup norms. This norm has the standard finite-coordinate topology.

The integral notation is the Bochner integral in the displayed space. It is totalized to zero when its integrand is not integrable. Reconstruct the literal assertions as displayed; do not add an integrability hypothesis or conclusion.
A local function G from the sample space to Prop defines a condition on a sample. The arrow following G omega is logical implication, with all subsequent conjunctions under its scope.

    if k.val = 0 then 1 else Real.sqrt 2 * Real.cos ((k.val : ℝ) * θ i)

    WithLp.toLp 2 (fun b : Fin (q + 1) => ω b i)

      Matrix (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) ℝ := fun i ω =>

    else 0

    ((∑ i : Fin d, w i • Z i ω) =
      (B ω).transpose * Matrix.diagonal w * B ω)

      _ = ((Real.sqrt (d : ℝ)) ^ 2)⁻¹ := by rw [pow_two, mul_inv]
      _ = _ := by rw [Real.sq_sqrt (by positivity)]

assumptions: Let \(d,q\in\mathbb N\), \(2q+1<d\), \(r=q+1\), and \(n=2q+1\). The case \(q=0\) is included; needed positivity follows internally.
On \(\Omega=(\mathbb R^d)^r\), use the original probability \(\mu=\gamma_d^{\otimes r}\), with \(\gamma_j=N(0,I_j)\). The actual physical row is \(\Phi_i=(\omega_{1,i},\ldots,\omega_{r,i})\).

Put \(\theta_i=(i-\tfrac12)\pi/d\), \(t_i=(1,\sqrt2\cos\theta_i,\ldots,\sqrt2\cos(q\theta_i))\), \(L=2r+3\log(1000d)\), and \(w_i=\cos(n\theta_i)\). For a Lean row index \(j:\mathrm{Fin}\,d\), the source row index is \(j.val+1\).

Define \(Y_i=d^{-1}(\Phi_i\Phi_i^\top\otimes t_it_i^\top)\mathbf1_{\{\|\Phi_i\|^2\le L\}}\), \(M_i=\int Y_i\,d\mu\), and \(Z_i=Y_i-M_i\). All means use the same original unconditional \(\mu\). The canonical actual-mean theorem establishes integrability internally.

Define the actual scalar \(a=r^{-1}\int_{\mathbb R^r}\|x\|^2\mathbf1_{\{\|x\|^2\le L\}}\,d\gamma_r(x)\). The actual matrix has entries \(B_{i,(b,k)}=d^{-1/2}\Phi_i(b)t_i(k)\), with the Gaussian coordinate first. Put \(D_n=\operatorname{diag}(w_i)\).

The source event \(\mathcal T=\{\omega:\|\Phi_i(\omega)\|^2\le L\text{ for every }i\}\) is denoted \(G\) in Lean. The public conclusion is pointwise on this inclusive event. Matrix norms are real Euclidean operator norms.

Private consumer only: for every real \(\Delta\), let \(\mathcal E_\Delta=\{\|\sum_iZ_i\|_{\rm op}\le\Delta,\ \|\sum_iw_iZ_i\|_{\rm op}\le\Delta\}\). The norm conclusion is on \(\mathcal T\cap\mathcal E_\Delta\). reconstruction.text:
For every pair of natural numbers \(d,q\), and every hypothesis \(h_q:2q+1<d\), make the following local definitions. All indices below are zero-based: \(\operatorname{Fin}(n)=\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\).

Let
\[
D=\operatorname{EuclideanSpace}_{\mathbb R}(\operatorname{Fin}(d)),\qquad
E=\operatorname{EuclideanSpace}_{\mathbb R}(\operatorname{Fin}(q+1)),\qquad
\Omega=\operatorname{Fin}(q+1)\to D.
\]
Thus \(D\) and \(E\) are real Euclidean spaces of dimensions \(d\) and \(q+1\), respectively. Write \(\gamma_D=\mathrm{stdGaussian}(D)\) and \(\gamma_E=\mathrm{stdGaussian}(E)\) for the centered Gaussian probability measures with identity covariance on those spaces. Define the measure on \(\Omega\) by
\[
\mu=\bigotimes_{b\in\operatorname{Fin}(q+1)}\gamma_D.
\]
Let the real numbers \(r,L\) be
\[
r=(q+1)\in\mathbb R,\qquad L=2r+3\log(1000d),
\]
where the natural numbers in real expressions are embedded into \(\mathbb R\), and \(\log\) is the natural logarithm. For \(i\in\operatorname{Fin}(d)\), define
\[
\theta_i=\frac{(i+1-\tfrac12)\pi}{d}.
\]
Define \(t:\operatorname{Fin}(d)\to\operatorname{Fin}(q+1)\to\mathbb R\) by
\[
t_{i,k}=\begin{cases}
1,&k=0,\\
\sqrt{2}\cos(k\theta_i),&k\ne0.
\end{cases}
\]
For each \(i\in\operatorname{Fin}(d)\) and \(\omega\in\Omega\), let
\[
\operatorname{row}_i(\omega)
=\bigl(\omega(b)_i\bigr)_{b\in\operatorname{Fin}(q+1)}\in E.
\]
This is precisely the Euclidean vector obtained by applying \(\mathrm{WithLp.toLp}\,2\) to the displayed coordinate function; \(\mathrm{WithLp.ofLp}\) recovers those same coordinates.

Define \(Y_i(\omega)\) to be a real square matrix with both its row and column index sets equal to
\(\operatorname{Fin}(q+1)\times\operatorname{Fin}(q+1)\), hence with dimension \((q+1)^2\) by \((q+1)^2\), as follows:
\[
Y_i(\omega)=
\begin{cases}
 d^{-1}\bigl[\operatorname{row}_i(\omega)\operatorname{row}_i(\omega)^{\mathsf T}\bigr]
 \otimes\bigl[t_i t_i^{\mathsf T}\bigr],
 &\|\operatorname{row}_i(\omega)\|_2^2\le L,\\
 0,&\|\operatorname{row}_i(\omega)\|_2^2>L.
\end{cases}
\]
Here the first outer product uses the coordinates recovered by \(\mathrm{WithLp.ofLp}\), the second uses the coordinate function \(t_i\), and \(\otimes\) is the matrix Kronecker product in this order. Explicitly, at row \((b,k)\) and column \((c,\ell)\), the entry in the first branch is
\[
 d^{-1}\,\omega(b)_i\,\omega(c)_i\,t_{i,k}\,t_{i,\ell}.
\]
The cutoff includes equality. Let
\[
\operatorname{mean}_i=\int_{\Omega}Y_i(\omega)\,d\mu(\omega),\qquad
Z_i(\omega)=Y_i(\omega)-\operatorname{mean}_i,
\]
with both matrices having that same pair index set. Define the real number
\[
a=\frac{1}{r}\int_E
 \mathbf 1_{\{y\in E:\|y\|_2^2\le L\}}(x)\,\|x\|_2^2\,d\gamma_E(x).
\]
The indicator is zero outside the displayed set and includes its boundary. Define \(w:\operatorname{Fin}(d)\to\mathbb R\) by
\[
w_i=\cos\bigl((2q+1)\theta_i\bigr).
\]
For each \(\omega\in\Omega\), define the real matrix \(B(\omega)\), with row index set \(\operatorname{Fin}(d)\) and column index set \(\operatorname{Fin}(q+1)\times\operatorname{Fin}(q+1)\), by
\[
 B(\omega)_{i,(b,k)}=(\sqrt d)^{-1}\,
 \bigl(\operatorname{row}_i(\omega)\bigr)_b\,t_{i,k}.
\]
Square roots are nonnegative square roots. Define the condition
\[
G(\omega)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \text{for every }i\in\operatorname{Fin}(d),\quad
 \|\operatorname{row}_i(\omega)\|_2^2\le L.
\]

Then, for every real number \(\Delta\) and every \(\omega\in\Omega\), if \(G(\omega)\) holds, the following implication holds:
\[
\left(
 \left\|\sum_{i\in\operatorname{Fin}(d)}Z_i(\omega)\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\Delta
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \left\|\sum_{i\in\operatorname{Fin}(d)}w_i Z_i(\omega)\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\Delta
\right)
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\left(
 \left\|B(\omega)^{\mathsf T}B(\omega)-I\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le\Delta+(1-a)
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \left\|B(\omega)^{\mathsf T}\operatorname{diag}(w)B(\omega)\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le\Delta
\right).
\]
In the conclusion, \(I\) is the identity matrix on
\(\operatorname{Fin}(q+1)\times\operatorname{Fin}(q+1)\), and \(\operatorname{diag}(w)\) is the \(d\)-by-\(d\) matrix whose diagonal entries are \(w_i\) and whose other entries are zero. Matrix products are ordinary matrix products; \(w_i Z_i(\omega)\) is real scalar multiplication. Every matrix norm displayed is the operator norm for the action between the corresponding Euclidean coordinate spaces. Every row-vector norm is the Euclidean norm.

Both integrals are Bochner integrals in their displayed spaces and are interpreted as zero if the integrand is not integrable; no integrability hypothesis or conclusion is imposed. The two norm inequalities in the antecedent must hold together, and the two norm inequalities in the conclusion are both under the hypotheses \(G(\omega)\) and that conjunction. No nonnegativity assumption is placed on \(\Delta\). The natural-number case \(q=0\) is included whenever \(1<d\).
